item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Oct 25–31
item.description: The biggest thing on the table this week is Tuesday's Telluride Town Council meeting, where the Fourth Supplement to the Gondola IGA goes up for a vote — that's the cost-sharing agreement that keeps 2027 planning money flowing on the gondola replacement — plus first readings of two ordinances touching the Energy Mitigation Program. Over in Ouray County, commissioners are deep into an EMS-Ridgway Fire merger discussion and a fifth extension of their Emergency Disaster Declaration, while the gondola's federal funding pursuit gets an airing Monday at the SMART Advisory Committee.

item.title: [Mon, Oct 26] Author Talk: Pam Houston
item.description:
🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride
Join us for a talk and signing with Pam Houston about her new book, Animals Taught Me Everything! What can a wagging tail and soaring wings teach us about a life well lived? From Icelandic mares and Irish wolfhounds to elephants, leopards, hyenas, and a desert-adapted lioness named Charlie, Pam Houston has learned life’s most important lessons from animals. How to play. How to rest. How to love. How to die. How to be present with the dying. How to be present with the living and with the Earth. How to find joy in the least likely places. How to find joy, literally, everywhere. With playful sincerity, Houston finds power and promise in the teachings of our fellow creatures and reminds us that animals are here for us, every day and everywhere.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Town Council - Oct 27 2026 — 2026-10-27
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-10-27
Three substantive items anchor this meeting. Council takes up the Fourth Supplement to the Gondola IGA, extending cost-sharing for the 2027 planning and development budget on the gondola replacement project — a line that connects directly to the SMART 3A funding voters approved. Two ordinances get first reading: one amending the Telluride Energy Mitigation Program (TEMP) under the municipal code, and one that would suspend the 5% capital fund allocation for open space in 2027 — a notable carve-out worth watching given the town's budget pressures. A work session covers special events on town property in 2026 and a proposed two-night concert in Town Park in August 2027. The long-running Stender Residence HARC appeal is continued again. Council also appoints an Open Space Commission member and approves routine minutes and a liquor licensing hearing officer.
⚡ Why it matters: Council votes on gondola IGA supplement and two ordinances get first reading.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Board of County Commissioners — 2026-10-27
item.description:
ouray • 2026-10-27
The Ouray County BOCC meets October 27 at the 4-H Event Center in Ridgway. The board takes up a fifth extension of the Emergency Disaster Declaration — a marker of how long the county has been navigating that situation. General business includes two vacancy-fill requests under the austerity resolution (Clerk and Recorder's Office, Treasurer's Office), a response letter on the Si Se Puede trademark dispute with UFW, a road materials supply agreement, and a resolution supporting Proposition 137 on the November 3 ballot. The board also considers a proclamation naming October 28 Gold Mountain Fire First Responder Appreciation Day. Sitting as the Local Licensing Authority, commissioners review a liquor license renewal for Divide Ranch. Sitting as the Board of Adjustment, they hold a public hearing on a Land Use Code variance request from Martha Campbell and the Home Trust of Ouray County for a property on County Road 24D. Blair & Associates presents the 2025 audited financial report.
⚡ Why it matters: Ouray BOCC votes on fifth Emergency Disaster Declaration extension and vacancy fills.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Board of County Commissioners Work Session — 2026-10-27
item.description:
ouray • 2026-10-27
A work session, so no formal votes — but the main business is consequential: commissioners take up the proposed merger of EMS and Ridgway Fire, with a budget and operational discussion followed by a preliminary draft agreement for BOCC input. Merging emergency services is the kind of structural decision that shapes response times, staffing, and costs for years. Commissioner and administrative reports fill the earlier part of the afternoon.
⚡ Why it matters: EMS and Ridgway Fire merger draft agreement shapes emergency response for years.

item.title: [Tue, Oct 27] Social Media for Nonprofits: Myth-Busting, Strategy & Practical Tips for Making Social Media Work for You
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride Social media can be a valuable tool for nonprofits, but there’s also a lot of pressure and misinformation about how to use it effectively. With changing algorithms, constant trends, and the expectation to post regularly, it can be difficult to know what really matters. This workshop will bust common social media myths, explore how these platforms can serve nonprofits differently than businesses, and share practical strategies for using social media as a tool for connection, storytelling, and community engagement without adding unnecessary pressure to your organization. Led by: Malarie Clark, Director of Marketing & Communications, Ah Haa School for the Arts & Shae LaPlace, Programming & Communications Manager, TMVOA Held at the Wilkinson Public Library Program Room -or- via Zoom Please register: https://forms.gle/BXfpSayGbNXPQDy2A

item.title: [Tue, Oct 27] America 250,Colorado 150 Book Club: Stampede to Timberline by Sibell Wolle
item.description:
🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride
This book includes the story of 240 of Colorado’s mining camps, with emphasis on the human side. The men who swarmed to the mountains to find precious metal came in successive waves from the late 1850s on, combing the gulches, scrambling over the passes and climbing the peaks. Their story is full of adventurous chances, lucky strikes, boom conditions, reckless spending, banditry, claim jumping, railroad wars and labor troubles. The author searched the Colorado Rockies from the time she saw and sketched her first ghost town until she had rediscovered and painted the vanishing mining camps. Twenty-two maps give the location of each one and serve as a guide for those who want to reach them by car or jeep, by horseback or on foot. …

item.description:
ouray • 2026-10-28
A work session — no formal votes — with two substantive conversations on the table. First, CDOT walks the commissioners through its annual planning presentation, covering what the state transportation agency has in store for the US-550 corridor and surrounding roads. Then the discussion shifts to FEMA Public Assistance, focusing on Ouray County's ongoing recovery projects and road damage assessments. Anyone who's watched mountain roads take a beating through wet cycles knows how long the repair queue can get — and how much of the funding story runs through federal reimbursement timelines.

item.title: [Thu, Oct 29] Coffee and Climate Conversations: The Super El Niño Is Here
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride Across our community, Super El Niño rumors are building hope and excitement that a snowy winter full of powder days is on the horizon. This year's El Niño is shaping up to be the strongest ever recorded, and is already driving changes in weather patterns, precipitation, and temperatures around the globe. Join us for a conversation with Emily Laidlaw, a social scientist at NOAA, to learn more about what the Super El Niño could mean for the San Juans and beyond, and how communities like ours could think about and prepare for its impacts.

item.title: [Fri, Oct 30] YOUNG FRANKENSTEIN – THE MUSICAL (a TMHS & Telluride Theatre Co-Production)
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Michael D. Palm Theater, Telluride It's okay to LAUGH during spooky season… we invite you to join us for Mel Brooks' classic comedy: YOUNG FRANKENSTEIN – THE MUSICAL! Based on the film starring Gene Wilder, this musical pokes fun at Mary Shelly's "Frankenstein," along with other classic monster movies. This production is performed and designed by our very own students at Telluride Middle-High School, under the mentorship of Telluride Theatre and the R-1 School District. Grandson of the infamous Victor Frankenstein, Frederick Frankenstein (pronounced "Fronk-en-steen") inherits his family's estate in Transylvania. With the help of a hunchbacked sidekick, Igor, and a yodeling lab assistant, Inga, Frederick finds himself in the mad scientist shoes of his ancestors. "It's alive!" he exclaims as he brings to life a creature to rival his grandfather's. Eventually, of course, the monster escapes, and hilarity ensues. Have a laugh this Halloween & support our local students. Costumes encouraged! …
